name: GraphQL query depth not limited
description:
The GraphQL endpoint executed a query nested ten object fields deep without a depth or complexity error. burpsy builds the query from the endpoint's own introspected schema: the shortest path from the query root to a type that refers back to itself, followed round that cycle until the query is ten fields deep. It never fans out - a list field is followed only through a first/limit-style argument set to 1 - so the probe itself costs the server ten small lookups.

A schema with a cycle (a category with a parent category, a user with friends who are users) admits queries of any depth, and with list fields each level multiplies the work of the one before it. Without a depth or cost limit, one small request can therefore make the server do an amount of work that grows exponentially with its nesting, which is a denial-of-service lever for anyone who can send a query.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's issue catalogue has no entry for GraphQL query depth. It is classified under CWE-770, Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. The probe needs introspection to find a cycle; on an endpoint with introspection disabled it is not run and nothing is reported either way.
remediation: Reject queries deeper than the application needs (a maximum depth in the GraphQL server, or a validation rule such as graphql-depth-limit), and prefer a query cost or complexity limit that also accounts for list sizes. Require pagination arguments with a server-side maximum on list fields, and set an execution timeout.
